source.title: Mind the Drift: Diagonal Linear Networks Under Large Learning Rates
source.authors: Aniket Sanyal; Tom Jacobs; Rebekka Burkholz

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present. Some figure text is garbled, and plotted values are not numerically recoverable.
record.tranche_reason: Extends large-learning-rate and edge-of-stability analysis to diagonal linear networks and sparse regression, reporting training outcomes; it does not test the classification-error claims in V1–V4 or the specific wide-network loss dynamics in V5.
record.gate_note: The paper reports diagonal-network sparse-recovery experiments, not benchmark classification error. Its plotted curves are not numerically recoverable, so figure-only values are recorded as such. The DeiT query-key analysis reports effective rank, a spectral-sparsity proxy rather than training error.
record.test_reason: The study's own full-batch GD experiments measure sharpness relative to the stability threshold in diagonal linear networks, bearing on V5's edge-of-stability component in a new setting. Sparse recovery and transformer effective rank do not themselves test any version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: Gain and Drift jointly shape solution selection in diagonal linear regression; aligned Drift can counteract Gain's preference for denser solutions. Gain Control improves sparse recovery in the tested settings, while extension to transformers remains exploratory.
record.recipe_differences: The work studies diagonal linear regression and introduces a Gain Control update; it does not use the original sources' benchmark classification recipes or evaluate training classification error.
record.method_sensitivity: Learning rate and whether training enters the oscillatory Edge of Stability regime change the sparse-versus-dense outcome; the paper also varies batch size and learning rate in its exploratory DeiT analysis.

fits_no_version.finding: At B=3.1, learning rate 0.3 produces a sparser predictor than 0.4, where continued Gain accumulation receives less compensation from Drift.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Learning rate can change sparse-versus-dense solution selection through competing Gain and Drift in diagonal linear regression.

fits_no_version.finding: Gain Control recovers the sparse teacher better than GD and SGD; at learning rate 0.1 it converges more slowly. Its recovery advantage also holds with cosine annealing.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Redistributing Gain can improve sparse recovery, with convergence-speed tradeoffs, in the tested diagonal regression settings.

fits_no_version.finding: The transformer configuration with the largest final Drift has the lowest query-key effective rank; the authors explicitly qualify this association as exploratory.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Gain and Drift measured in an initialization-fixed frame may be associated with transformer query-key spectral concentration.

record.problems: The main quantitative sparse-recovery curves are figure-only in the supplied text; their values cannot be recovered. The transformer analysis is explicitly exploratory, uses a fixed initialization frame, and the authors caution that rotation of singular subspaces and Muon's non-coordinatewise updates limit its validation of the theory.

untested.parts: Training classification error in convolutional networks on CIFAR, including corrupted labels and model-size comparisons.
Spurious minima in ReLU teacher-student networks and the effect of extra student neurons.
Depth degradation, identity shortcuts, and training very deep plain or unnormalized residual networks.
Activation-matched initialization, signal propagation, training speed, and trainable depth.

Recovery above the initial linearized stability limit, the initial loss rise and curvature drop, divergence at larger rates, and divergence from below the threshold. Sustained loss decline concurrent with threshold hovering at a fixed learning rate cannot be established from the supplied curve text; the main regression experiment reduces its learning rate after 500 epochs.
Batch normalization comparisons and Fixup training speed and stability.

missing.what: Separate sharpness results for full-batch GD: at B=3.1, learning rate 0.3 converges below the threshold while 0.4 oscillates around it. Record the plotted sharpness-times-step-size measure separately from sparsity.
Record the full-batch GD sharpness trajectory showing onset of threshold oscillations, with Gain continuing to accumulate while Drift changes little. Exact plotted values are unavailable.

record.verdict_notes: Failure to recover the sparse teacher is not failure to fit the training data. Neither that distinction nor the learning-rate reduction establishes a challenge to V5. The study is not an original source for any version.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR classification error, random or corrupted labels, model size, optimizer, and training duration.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student networks, spurious minima, and student width relative to teacher width.
Plain versus residual convolutional networks and their training classification error.
Activation-matched initialization, signal and gradient propagation, and trainable depth.

The stated wide-network setting and loss trajectory above the initial linearized stability limit are not tested. The paper studies diagonal linear networks and does not textually report the specified brief loss rise followed by low loss.
Batch normalization versus no normalization, speed of accuracy gain, and learning-rate tolerance.

relationships.reason: R3's accompanying text reports threshold oscillations; the omitted sharpness results in Figures 3 and 9 independently document the edge-of-stability component. This verdict rests on the text and captions, not recovered numerical curves.
